sources.title: July 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
sources.lines: overview and contract table; snapshot held 16 July 2026
facts: BDUK publishes this as monthly contract-level management information for Project Gigabit.
The table is a snapshot of data held on 16 July 2026 and is rounded to the nearest ten.
Contracted premises cover initial contract scope and can exclude deferred scope.
BDUK states these figures are not directly comparable with its official-statistics delivery totals.
Contracted or built management status is not evidence that retail service is currently orderable at an exact UPRN.

sources.title: June 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
sources.lines: overview and contract table; snapshot held 17 June 2026
facts: The June release is monthly contract-level management information published by BDUK.
The table is a snapshot of data held on 17 June 2026 and values are rounded to the nearest ten.
The release reports 839,340 contracted premises and 271,460 built contracted premises in total.
BDUK warns that ingestion lag means the table should not be used to assess contractual milestones.
Built contracted premises remain distinct from subsidy-attributed official statistics and exact current retail availability.

sources.title: December 2025: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
facts: This is a BDUK monthly contract-progress publication for December 2025.
The publication is transparency or management information rather than an official-statistics delivery bulletin.
Values are rounded and contract scope must be retained when comparing releases.
Historic contract snapshots can be revised as supplier administrative records change.
A historic built count cannot be promoted to current parcel service without exact UPRN and orderability evidence.

sources.title: November 2025: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
facts: This page is the November 2025 monthly Project Gigabit contract-progress release.
The data is rounded to the nearest ten and totals may not sum because of rounding.
Contract progress is administrative evidence with a specific reporting vintage.
Supplier or scope revisions can change values between monthly publications.
Contract-level built status is not an exact address-level statement of live retail service.

sources.title: October 2025: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
facts: This was the first monthly document in the Project Gigabit contracted-and-built collection.
It reports contract-level management information for an October 2025 vintage.
Rounded counts and contract definitions must be preserved in downstream comparisons.
The release should not be mixed directly with BDUK official-statistics subsidy delivery totals.
Parcel promotion remains blocked without exact UPRN linkage and current service evidence.

sources.title: Premises contracted and built, Project Gigabit contracts
sources.lines: collection document list and update history
facts: The collection publishes monthly updates for October 2025 through July 2026.
BDUK describes the series as numbers of premises contracted and built under each Project Gigabit contract.
The collection was first published on 24 October 2025 and updated on 20 July 2026.
Monthly management information and official-statistics delivery measures use different definitions.
The collection index identifies releases but does not itself prove service availability at any premise.

sources.title: Building Digital UK performance information
facts: The collection separates BDUK official statistics from Project Gigabit monthly contract reports.
It lists the annual April 2025 to March 2026 official-statistics release dated 11 June 2026.
It links the contracted-and-built transparency series updated on 20 July 2026.
Different programme measures and reporting periods must remain separate in lineage.
A collection-level entry is contextual evidence, not exact parcel availability.

sources.title: January 2026 OMR and premises in BDUK plans (England and Wales)
sources.lines: publication metadata, downloads and accessibility note
facts: The publication supplies January 2026 OMR and premises-in-BDUK-plans material for England and Wales.
It includes a UPRN-level release and a user guide or technical note.
OMR and plan status are administrative planning classifications with a defined vintage.
Planned or classified premises must remain distinct from built and currently orderable service.
UPRN-level identifiers enable exact joins but do not remove the need for current service validation.

sources.title: UPRN level release user guide and technical note for premises in BDUK plans — January 2026
facts: The guide documents interpretation of the January 2026 UPRN-level BDUK plans release.
It is a methodology and field-use source rather than a live retail service checker.
Release vintage, plan status and programme scope must be retained with each UPRN.
Administrative plan membership cannot be treated as completed build.
Current parcel promotion requires an exact UPRN plus separately verified orderable-service evidence.

sources.title: September 2025 OMR and premises in BDUK plans (England and Wales)
facts: The publication provides a September 2025 OMR and BDUK-plan snapshot for England and Wales.
It contains UPRN-level data and associated interpretation guidance.
The September vintage must not be silently substituted for January 2026 or current status.
OMR classification expresses market and intervention planning evidence.
Parcel service truth remains gated by exact identity, current date and orderability.

sources.title: UPRN level release user guide and technical note for premises in BDUK plans — September 2025
facts: This guide supports the September 2025 UPRN-level BDUK plans release.
It provides technical context for interpreting plan and OMR records.
The guide does not convert planned status into proof of completed network delivery.
Historical UPRN records require explicit vintage and lineage when compared with later releases.
Exact UPRN matching is necessary but not sufficient for a current service claim.

sources.title: May 2025 OMR and premises in BDUK plans (England and Wales)
facts: The May 2025 publication is an earlier OMR and BDUK-plan snapshot for England and Wales.
It links UPRN-level data and a user guide or technical note.
Comparisons with September 2025 and January 2026 require explicit version control.
OMR data describes commercial or intervention planning status rather than guaranteed service.
Historic plan records cannot be promoted to current parcel truth without fresh evidence.

sources.title: UPRN level release user guide and technical note for premises in BDUK plans — May 2025
facts: The linked guide explains the May 2025 UPRN-level plans release.
It is a methodology source and should be stored separately from the data snapshot.
Field definitions and plan classifications must be preserved during ingestion.
A plan record may change in later OMR releases and therefore needs versioned lineage.
Exact current orderability remains a separate parcel-promotion gate.
